DexArena documentation

Understand the benchmark, follow the research workflows, and cite the DexArena preprint.

A benchmark for skills and complete sequences

DexArena evaluates long-horizon dexterous manipulation through 10 long-horizon tasks and 30 stage-level tasks. The stages expose individual skills; the complete tasks test whether those skills work in sequence, including bimanual coordination and transitions. Task success comes from physical environment predicates, including the task's persistent hold or latch conditions.

Start with the task catalog to choose an environment and understand its stage boundaries. The benchmark overview illustrates the task families, while the results compare the six methods evaluated in the manuscript.

What is available today

ArtifactCurrent status
PaperarXiv:2611.02629 ↗ and public PDF ↗; a 2026 preprint.
Official repositorySIPAIR-Elastic/DexArena ↗. The current public tree contains the README, Apache 2.0 license and repository metadata; the runnable research package is not published there yet.
DemonstrationsThe paper reports 3,000 replay-successful episodes. A public dataset download endpoint has not been supplied.
Trained policiesThe manuscript reports baseline results. Public DexArena checkpoint download endpoints have not been supplied.
Evaluation intakeThe site presents manuscript baseline results. Public community submission intake is not open.

The installation and execution examples in this center describe verified interfaces in the research source. They become usable when you already have that source, its assets and compatible dependencies. See Resources & release status before planning a reproduction run.

Follow a complete workflow

  1. Prepare a research checkout, verify the task registry, and create one canonical environment.
  2. Read the configuration contract and run the small wiring check.
  3. Inspect demonstrations and replay, then choose a baseline or implement a policy adapter.
  4. Freeze the checkpoint and evaluate native-scene transfer and complete sequences with the registered task definitions.
  5. Save the reproduction artifacts, calculate task-weighted metrics, and cite the benchmark.

Read each score in its own setting

TrackEvaluation unitQuestion
Stage execution30 stages; 50 episodes per stage in the training sceneCan the policy complete an individual skill from its valid stage reset?
Cross-scene generalization30 stages × 3 native scenes; 50 episodes per pairDoes the frozen policy transfer across the named kitchen scenes?
Long-horizon composition10 sequences; 50 episodes per sequenceCan the policy finish the complete sequence after a single reset?

Stage completion does not imply complete-sequence success. Keep task horizons, success predicates and stage-transition rules fixed. The score protocol explains aggregation and the meaning of scene variation.
